title: Regional backpressure and model ladder playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook for a complementary approach to graceful degradation that emphasizes: regional backpressure signals, a model-quality ladder (model variants ordered by cost/latency/quality), and explicit spillover policies that preserve high-priority traffic while minimizing user-visible regressions. Intended audience: platform eng, serving runtime, and SRE.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Treat each region as an independent capacity silo with soft admission controls.
- Emit a compact backpressure signal (BPscore) per region that represents short-window utilization + request mix.
- Route by policy: prefer local high-quality model, fall back to cheaper variant within region, then spill to remote region only if BPscore above threshold AND request priority permits.
- Prioritize interactive low-latency requests over background/async workloads during degradation windows.
- Implement circuit-breaker + gradual ramp-down for model swaps to avoid mass regen/latency spikes.

Design goals / constraints:
- Minimize cross-region latency blast radius. Avoid flooding remote regions.
- Keep deterministic routing behavior for reproducibility (important for experiments/rollouts).
- Make degradation minimally invasive to developer experience: same API, but consistent probability of variant selection under load.
- Observability first: every spillover path must surface metrics + traces and tie back to SLOs and cost.

Key concepts and knobs:
- BPscore: scalar 0..100 computed every 5s from: GPU utilization, pending queue length, avg response latency (p50/p95), soft capsule for token/sec. Tunable weights.
- Model ladder: an ordered list for each primary model (e.g., rwd-xl-v2 -> rwd-xl-quant8 -> rwd-xl-llmf -> rwd-xl-8k-trim). Each variant has metadata: expected p50, p95, cost-per-token, compatible-kernel-tag.
- Admission classes: real-time (interactive), streaming, batch/async. Admission policy matrix decides which classes can be shed.
- Spillover budget: a per-region token budget that limits outgoing forwarded requests per minute to remote regions. Prevents stampeding other regions.

Routing policy (sketch):
- On request arrival: tag request with priority and model family.
- Look up region state (BPscore, local-variants-healthy, spillover-remaining).
- If BPscore < degrade_threshold_low -> route to local top model.
- If BPscore in [low, high): try local next variant in ladder that meets latency SLO. If none, consult spillover policy: allow X% of interactive requests to remote top-model until spillover_budget depleted.
- If BPscore >= degrade_threshold_high: enforce admission control: throttle async, convert streaming to chunked-mode, accept only highest priority interactive and route them to local cheaper variants or remote top-model if allowed.

Control plane responsibilities:
- Maintain zone/regional BPscore aggregation and historical windows (5s/1m/5m).
- Distribute model ladder metadata (compatible kernels, quantization flags, feature flags for fallback).
- Coordinate spillover budgets and lease-style grants for temporary extra capacity in remote regions (timeboxed).
- Provide an API for SRE/product to set per-customer or per-route priorities and override fallbacks for high-value customers.

Implementation notes / runtime mechanics:
- Small centralized controller (k8s operator) pushes BPscore -> regional agents. Agents keep a tiny in-memory policy table and respond to route queries (fast path).
- Use probabilistic selection during transitional states (e.g., 20% of interactive routed to cheaper variant) to A/B test regression impact gradually. Record per-prompt quality signals where available.
- KV cache and prefix caching should be invalidated only when moving to a different model family; prefer variants that share KV-format to preserve cache hit rate. Ladder must declare KV-compatibility tag.
- Circuit-breaker: when a variant swap causes p95 > X or error-rate spike, roll requests back to previous variant and mark variant unhealthy for T minutes. Avoid immediate fallback to remote region to prevent cyclical traffic shifting.

Observability/alerts:
- Core metrics: BPscore, spillover-rate, variant-selection-rate, per-variant p50/p95, per-route SLO violations, spillover-cost.
- Alerts: sustained BPscore>threshold_high for 2m, spillover_rate > budget for 1m, cross-region latency tail spike.
- Dashboards: region overview, model-ladder heatmap (how often variants are used under load), per-customer degradation exposure.

Playbook (runbook steps for an SRE during regional overload):
1) Identify root region via BPscore dashboard. 2) Check recent deploys/PRs that touched model ladder or kernel selection (linked PRs). 3) If BPscore rising: enable conservative admission (shed async) and throttle non-business-critical routes. 4) If user-impact visible: enable regional canary of cheaper variant for <10% traffic and monitor quality regressions. 5) If still overloaded, enable limited spillover to nearest region using spillover budget. 6) If cross-region spillover causes remote degradation, rollback spillover and revisit admission. 7) After pressure subsides, ramp variants back to top model progressively (reverse of prob selection schedule).

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- How to compute BPscore weights for mixed CPU/GPU shapes? Need experiment to correlate BPscore with observed p95 regressions.
- What is fair default spillover budget? Start with 1-2% of regional peak throughput and tune.
- Integration with Dedicated reserved capacity: reserved pools should have preemptive admission priority; adjust BPscore to incorporate reserved pool headroom.
- UX in Console: show "degradation band" and which variant is active with timestamps.

Short checklist for next steps:
- [ ] Prototype BPscore agent (5s window, GPU util + p95).
- [ ] Define ladder metadata schema (KV-compat, cost, expected latency).
- [ ] Add small controller API for spillover leases.
- [ ] Write chaos test that simulates sudden regional capacity drop and asserts no more than 5% of requests go to any single remote region.
- [ ] Add unit tests for probabilistic variant selector.

Appendix: sample variant metadata line (format for model-catalog entry):
- model_family: rwd-xl-v2
- variant_id: rwd-xl-v2-quant8
- quality_rank: 2
- expected_p50_ms: "120"
- expected_p95_ms: "300"
- cost_per_token: "0.0023"
- kv_compatible: "true"
- kernel_tags: ["cuda-11-9", "triton-optimized"]

Links and references: see linked_artifacts. Also internal thread: #platform-regional-degrade on Slack.

Notes: this is a working draft — lots of rough edges. Aim to formalize into a spec and a small prototype in Q1 2025.
